note: R25: practice set A, written without access to the frozen test

stories.text: The pharmacist, Darius, closed his counter at one o'clock every day to eat lunch in the park. On Monday a girl named Fumiko came running in just before one because her grandmother needed cough syrup. Darius stayed open ten more minutes and found the bottle on the top shelf. Fumiko thanked him and ran home with it while he locked the door.
qs: Where did Darius find the bottle?
When did Darius usually close his counter?
What did Darius do while Fumiko ran home?

stories.text: A tortoise named Kelo wanted to see the sea, but it was three hills away. He asked a gull to carry him, and the gull said she was too small. Then a goat, who was going to the shore for salt, let Kelo ride on his back. By sunset the tortoise was standing in the cold foam, and the goat was licking the rocks.
qs: Who wanted to see the sea?
What did Kelo ask the gull to do?
Who let Kelo ride on his back?
What was the goat doing by sunset?
Where was the tortoise by sunset?

stories.text: At eight, Liang left the bakery with a crate of rolls and drove to the school. He left half the rolls in the school kitchen and took the rest to the hospital on Birch Road. The hospital cook, Mrs Bello, signed for them at ten. Before noon Liang was back at the bakery, washing the empty crate.
qs: Who left the bakery at eight?
Where did Liang take the rest of the rolls?
Who signed for the rolls at the hospital?
When did Mrs Bello sign for the rolls?
What was Liang washing before noon?

stories.text: Hedda fixed bicycles in a small shed behind her house. One rainy afternoon her neighbour Behrouz brought a bike with a bent wheel, and she told him to come back on Friday. Behrouz's son, Emre, could not wait, so he borrowed his cousin's scooter to get to football practice. On Friday the wheel was straight and Behrouz paid with a jar of honey.
qs: Who brought a bike with a bent wheel?

stories.text: A mouse and a mole shared a burrow under a turnip field. The mouse gathered seeds all summer, while the mole only slept and dug. When winter came, the mouse's store was eaten by beetles, but the mole's deep tunnels were full of worms. The mole shared his worms, and the mouse learned that digging was work too.
qs: Where did the mouse and the mole live?
What did the mouse gather all summer?
What were the mole's tunnels full of?

stories.text: Carmen packed her suitcase on Tuesday night and caught the early train to Lisbon. In Lisbon she left the suitcase at her aunt's flat and walked to the harbour. Her aunt, Beatriz, met her there with two tickets for the ferry. That evening the suitcase was still in the flat, but Carmen and Beatriz were eating fish across the river.
qs: Who packed a suitcase on Tuesday night?
Who met Carmen at the harbour?
What did Beatriz have for the ferry?
When did Carmen pack her suitcase?
Where was the suitcase that evening?

stories.text: A water pipe burst under Hollin Street on Saturday morning, and several shops were flooded. The owner of the shoe shop, Kwabena Asante, carried his boxes up to the attic. Firefighters pumped the water out by the afternoon. The street was closed until Monday while the pipe was repaired by city workers.
qs: Where did Kwabena carry his boxes?
What did Kwabena carry up to the attic?

stories.text: A young fox boasted that he could catch the moon in the pond. Every night he jumped into the water, and every night the moon broke into pieces and floated back together. An old heron watched him from the reeds. At last she told him, 'The moon you want is in the sky, and the one in the pond belongs to the pond.'
qs: Who boasted that he could catch the moon?
What did the fox do every night?
Where did the heron watch from?
What broke into pieces every night?

stories.text: On Sunday morning Gustavo took his grandson Ali to the market to buy a goose. They carried it home in a basket, but at the bridge the goose escaped and ran into the river. Ali waded in after it while his grandfather held the basket. By lunchtime the goose was in the yard, and Ali's shoes were drying by the stove.
qs: Who took Ali to the market?
What did they buy at the market?
What did the goose do at the bridge?
Where were Ali's shoes by lunchtime?

stories.text: Dr Ifeoma Chukwu runs the only clinic in Ebute village. Because the road floods in April, she keeps a canoe tied behind the clinic. Last spring a farmer named Jabu cut his hand while she was away visiting her sister. His wife paddled him across in the doctor's canoe, and Dr Chukwu stitched the hand when she returned that night.
qs: Where does she keep a canoe?
Why does Dr Chukwu keep a canoe?
When did Dr Chukwu stitch the hand?

stories.text: A crow and a pig both wanted the last apple on the tree. The pig shook the trunk, but the apple held fast. The crow pecked the stem until it snapped, and the apple dropped into the mud beside the pig. The pig ate it in one bite, and the crow learned to pick her partners more carefully.
qs: What did the crow and the pig both want?

stories.text: The red kettle sat on the stove in Amira's kitchen until noon. At noon her brother Farid took it to the garden to fill the bird bath. He forgot it there, and in the evening Amira found it under the plum tree full of rainwater. She carried it back inside and put it on the windowsill to dry.
qs: What did Farid forget in the garden?
Who took the kettle to the garden?
Why did Farid take the kettle to the garden?
Who found the kettle in the evening?
Where was the kettle at the end?

stories.text: Every Thursday the librarian, Mr Haruto Abe, reads stories to the children in the back room. This week the projector broke, so a boy named Diego held up the pictures instead. Diego's little sister, Asel, sat in the front row and laughed at every page. After the reading, Mr Abe gave each child a paper bookmark.
qs: What did Mr Abe give each child?

stories.text: A beaver built a dam across a stream, and the frogs below it grumbled that their pool was drying up. The beaver ignored them until a heavy storm came. That night the dam held back the flood, and the frogs' pool was the only one in the valley that did not overflow. In the morning the frogs brought the beaver a bundle of willow sticks.
qs: When did the frogs bring the beaver a gift?
What did the frogs bring the beaver?

stories.text: Kamal started his day at the post office, where he picked up forty letters. He delivered most of them on Elm Street before ten. One letter was for a house that had been empty for a year, so he took it back to the post office. Late in the afternoon he cycled to the farm at the end of the valley with a parcel for Mrs Halvorsen.
qs: Where did Kamal deliver most of the letters?
How many letters did Kamal pick up?
Where did Kamal cycle late in the afternoon?

stories.text: Bianca and her husband, Joaquin, opened a small cafe across from the train station. She baked the cakes, and he made the coffee. On their first morning a storm knocked out the power, and the coffee machine stopped. Joaquin boiled water on a camping stove, and the customers drank their coffee by candlelight.
qs: What did Joaquin boil water on?

stories.text: A hen found a shiny button in the yard and believed it was gold. She hid it in her nest and refused to lay eggs, because she was too busy guarding it. The farmer's dog laughed and told her that buttons cannot hatch. Ashamed, the hen dropped the button into the well and went back to laying.
qs: Where did the hen hide the button?
What did the hen do with the button at the end?
Why did the hen refuse to lay eggs?

stories.text: At dawn the ferry left the island with Captain Dora Ferro at the wheel and a cargo of lemons. It reached the mainland port by nine, where the lemons were unloaded into trucks. The captain bought fuel and newspapers and sailed back after lunch. By evening the newspapers were being read in the island's only bar.
qs: Who was at the wheel of the ferry?
When did the ferry reach the mainland port?
When did the captain sail back?
Where were the newspapers by evening?

stories.text: When the school bus broke down on the hill, the driver, Gintaras, phoned the head teacher. The head teacher, Ms Okoro, sent the gym teacher with the school van. The van could carry only nine children, so it made three trips. The last group reached school at half past nine, just in time for the spelling test.
qs: Who was the driver of the school bus?
What did Ms Okoro send the gym teacher with?
What broke down on the hill?
When did the last group reach school?

stories.text: A lazy cat lived in a mill full of mice. Instead of hunting, she made a deal with the mice: they could eat the spilled flour if they kept the rats away. The miller saw no mice in the daytime and praised the cat. But one night he came down with a lamp and found the cat asleep on a sack while the mice swept the floor.
qs: Who made a deal with the mice?
What did the mice have to keep away?

stories.text: Before breakfast Joelle hung the wet sheets on the line behind the guesthouse. At eleven the wind blew one sheet over the fence into the sheep field. A shepherd named Anwar brought it back folded over his arm. By three o'clock all the sheets were dry and back on the beds upstairs.
qs: Who hung the sheets on the line?
What blew a sheet over the fence?
When did the sheet blow away?
Where were the sheets by three o'clock?

stories.text: Hakim sells newspapers from a green kiosk outside the cinema. On rainy days his daughter Leila brings him soup in a flask at noon. Last week a film star stopped to buy a paper and left her umbrella on the counter. Hakim kept it behind the kiosk for three days until her driver came to collect it.
qs: What did the film star leave on the counter?
Who came to collect the umbrella?

stories.text: A snail wanted to visit the fair in the next village, which lasted only one day. Knowing she was slow, she set off a whole month early. Along the way a rabbit laughed at her and said he would leave the day before. The rabbit overslept and missed the fair, but the snail arrived on the morning it opened.
qs: Who wanted to visit the fair?
When did the snail set off?
Why did the rabbit miss the fair?

stories.text: On Monday the museum's blue vase was sent from the storeroom to a workshop to be cleaned. The restorer, Dagny, worked on it for two days. On Thursday it was returned to the museum and placed in the glass case by the entrance. A guard named Cyrus checks the case every hour.
qs: What was sent to the workshop?
Where was the vase before Monday?
Where was the vase placed on Thursday?
Who checks the case every hour?

stories.text: Kiri's grandfather was a fisherman, and he taught her to tie knots on the porch. When she was twelve, she entered a sailing race on the lake. Her boat lost its rudder halfway, but she steered with an oar and finished fourth. Her grandfather, who had watched from the jetty, cheered louder than anyone.
qs: Who taught Kiri to tie knots?
How old was Kiri when she entered the race?
Where did her grandfather watch the race from?

stories.text: A bear found a beehive in a hollow log and wanted the honey. The bees stung his nose, so he asked a badger for advice. The badger told him to wait until night, when the bees were asleep. The bear waited, ate the honey in the dark, and woke the next day with a sticky but unstung face.
qs: Who did the bear ask for advice?
What did the bear do after waiting?
When did the bear eat the honey?

stories.text: Elena's map of the old town started the day in her backpack. At the cathedral she gave it to a lost tourist, a man named Florin, who was looking for the river. Florin left the map on a bench by the river when he sat down to eat. In the afternoon a street cleaner picked it up and pinned it to the notice board at the tourist office.
qs: Who had the map after Elena gave it away?
Where did Elena give the map away?
Where did Florin leave the map?
Who picked up the map in the afternoon?
Where was the map at the end?

stories.text: Babajide drives a taxi at night and sleeps until noon. His upstairs neighbour, Mrs Jankowska, practises the piano every morning. Instead of complaining, Babajide bought earplugs, and she started playing only after eleven. Now they share a pot of tea on Sundays.
qs: What does Babajide drive at night?
When does Mrs Jankowska play the piano now?
What do they share on Sundays?

stories.text: A peacock and a sparrow were caught in a net set by a hunter. The peacock spread his tail and screamed, which only tangled him further. The sparrow kept still and slipped through a torn corner. Before the hunter returned, she came back with a mouse, who chewed through the cords and set the peacock free.
qs: What did the peacock do in the net?
Who slipped through a torn corner?
What did the mouse chew through?

stories.text: Leon's school trip began at the zoo, where the class watched the penguins being fed at nine. Then the bus took them to the science museum, and they ate their sandwiches on its steps. At two they visited the planetarium next door. Leon left his cap on the bus, and the driver, Abebe, kept it for him until Monday.
qs: What did the class watch at the zoo?
When did the class visit the planetarium?
Where did Leon leave his cap?
What did the class eat on the museum steps?

stories.text: Aditi runs a stall that repairs phones in the covered market. Her assistant, Collins, is very fast but often loses the small screws. On Wednesday a customer's screw rolled under the stall, and Collins spent an hour looking for it. Aditi found it in the end with a magnet tied to a stick.
qs: Who often loses the small screws?
What did Collins do on Wednesday?
How did Aditi find the screw?

stories.text: A hedgehog and a hare both wanted to sleep in the same dry hollow during a storm. The hare said he was faster and had arrived first, but the hedgehog had slept there for years. An owl suggested they share it, the hare at the front and the hedgehog at the back. By morning the hare was grateful, because the hedgehog's spines had kept a hungry weasel away.
qs: What did the hedgehog and the hare both want to sleep in?

stories.text: Ji-woo's suitcase was checked in at Seoul and should have flown with her to Frankfurt. Instead it was put on a plane to Helsinki by mistake. It reached Frankfurt a day later, where a courier, Hendrik, drove it to her hotel. By then Ji-woo had already bought a new toothbrush.
qs: Where was the suitcase checked in?
Where was the suitcase sent by mistake?
Who drove the suitcase to her hotel?
When did the suitcase reach Frankfurt?

stories.text: The town's oldest baker, Lorenzo, retired this spring after fifty years. His apprentice, Giulietta, took over the shop on Bell Street. On her first day the bread came out flat, because she had forgotten the salt. Lorenzo, who still came by for coffee, tasted it and laughed.
qs: Why did the bread come out flat?
How many years had Lorenzo been a baker?

stories.text: A young owl was afraid of the dark, which is a problem for an owl. Her mother sent her to the glow-worms at the edge of the marsh. The glow-worms lit a path for her every night for a week. By the end of the week the owl was flying alone, and the glow-worms had a friend who kept the frogs from eating them.
qs: Who was afraid of the dark?
Who sent the owl to the glow-worms?
What did the glow-worms do for the owl?
Who did the owl keep from eating the glow-worms?

stories.text: Gabriel and his sister Lidia went fishing on the lake at six in the morning. By eight they had caught nothing, so they rowed to the far shore near the old boathouse. There Lidia caught a trout, and Gabriel caught a boot. They were home by noon, and the trout was cooked for lunch while the boot was hung on the shed.
qs: Where did they row at eight?

stories.text: A lost parrot was returned to its owner in Dunmore on Friday after three weeks away. The bird, called Kiwi, had been living in the bell tower of the church. The bell ringer, Augustin, heard it whistling a pop song and called the local radio station. The owner, a retired nurse, recognised the song at once.
qs: What was returned to its owner?

stories.text: A proud rooster crowed every morning and believed his voice made the sun rise. One day he caught a cold and could not crow at all. He hid in the barn, but when he peeked out the sun was already shining. A goose passing by told him the sun had never needed his help.
qs: Who believed his voice made the sun rise?
Why could the rooster not crow?
Who told the rooster the sun never needed his help?
What was the sun doing when the rooster peeked out?

stories.text: The library's only copy of a cookbook was borrowed by Kasia on the first of May. She lent it to her flatmate Duc, who took it to his parents' house in the country. His mother copied six recipes and posted the book back to the city. It was returned to the library on the twentieth, two days late.
qs: Who borrowed the cookbook from the library?
Who had the cookbook after Kasia lent it?
Where did Duc take the cookbook?
How many recipes did Duc's mother copy?
When was the cookbook returned to the library?

stories.text: Every evening Faisal walks the neighbour's dog, Biscuit, because the neighbour, old Mr Larsen, has a bad knee. Yesterday Biscuit pulled free and chased a cat into the churchyard. Faisal found him tangled in a rosebush and carried him home. Mr Larsen thanked Faisal with a slice of cake.
qs: Who walks the dog every evening?
What did Mr Larsen thank Faisal with?
